data.title: bn-168k: Resolve trusted verification slots and native plan budgets
data.description: Review the passive plan only. The canonical resolver accepts operator-owned principal pins, checks lead and preview conflicts, and preserves unsupported-class and fixed-slot refusals. The plan derives the conservative compiled request bound and reports native units separately after checking the pinned pass before and after the dry run. Custody and enforcement come from the selected runtime path and observation, and positive-status ceiling comes from accepted policy and owner provenance. Focused offline tests, all-target/all-feature strict Clippy, and full serialized offline just check passed on this source. No live fixture verification was run.

data.body: HIGH: The preview uses engine units as the pass-wide allowance for the compiled recipe. `native_budget` compares `plan.required_requests` to macro `run.units_left`. The accounting adapter records that value as Granularity::Engine (teapot/accounting.rs:561-570). Live `preflight_registered` uses it to check the macro itself, then compares the full compiled bound to pass-level `pass show` `requests.left` and requires a present `spent` (teapot/accounting.rs:357-395, 529-535). An engine dry run can therefore report `compiled_requests_fit=true` with insufficient or missing pass allowance. It can also report BUDGET_REFUSED when the macro fits its engine ceiling and the pass has sufficient allowance. Preserve native macro units as their own reading and derive the compiled fit and blocker from the same passive pass-ledger inputs and predicates as live admission. Cover disagreement in both directions plus unavailable pass counters.

MEDIUM: The plan projects a target-isolation claim from distinct session references alone. The predicate sees only whether both roles have a `verifier_session`. The CLI emits the result as `experiment.target_isolation` at lead.rs:748, where consumers cannot see the internal session-layout qualification. Two distinct session names can authenticate to the same account used during exploration. The frozen meaning of `separate_principals_unconfined` requires distinct target accounts (docs/adr/custody-topology.md:45-52 and notes/plan.md:268-275). Represent the configured verifier-session layout explicitly while keeping actual target isolation unestablished or explicitly hypothetical pending account observations. Cover the case where separate session names do not establish separate accounts.

LOW: The CLI drops action cardinality when projecting the registered flow plan. `flows_per_round` contains each dispatch name once, while `operations.rs:190-194` defines two `C` actions per round. The CLI therefore reports twelve flow names but has no way to show the thirteen scheduled recipe actions or their distribution. `compiled_requests_per_round` is a separate conservative budget that includes possible retry and login sends. Keep the existing names and expose each dispatch action count or the base per-round action count alongside them.

data.body: Fixed: the preview and live admission share the registered-capacity predicate. Macro engine units are an independent observation. The compiled fit uses validated pass-wide spent and left counters for the exact pinned pass, with separate budget and unestablished blockers. Offline cases cover both directions of disagreement, engine refusal, and absent counters.

Fixed: configured_sessions records each selected role source and target_isolation is unestablished before account observations. The offline regression shows distinct configured native session names with a null target-isolation projection.

Fixed: JSON retains ordered flow names and reports per-dispatch counts plus the per-round action sum alongside the compiled request bound. The registry regression covers twelve dispatches, thirteen actions, and two C actions. The CLI regression asserts their separate output fields.

Verified on e5f6bcad25cf4dc414d51efc2e29fb1f7e26025a. planning.rs:408–440 and teapot/accounting.rs:352–379 share registered_capacity. The engine macro checks its own fit. The compiled recipe gates on validated pass-wide spent and left from the latest sample, after validating the pinned path and digest and matching the pre-dry-run pass ID and enforcement. Re-ran the offline regression for both directions of engine-versus-ledger disagreement, engine refusal, and unavailable counters, plus seven existing accounting adapter tests.

Verified on e5f6bcad25cf4dc414d51efc2e29fb1f7e26025a. planning.rs:184–201 and lead.rs:748–750 report configured session sources by role and leave target isolation unestablished. The offline regression passed with distinct alice_verify and bob_verify session names and no target-isolation claim.

Verified on e5f6bcad25cf4dc414d51efc2e29fb1f7e26025a. lead.rs:765–789 preserves registry order and reports twelve dispatches, thirteen actions, and two C actions per round, with distinct conservative compiled request fields. The registry and JSON projection regressions passed.
